A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same length-collapse analysis and TempScale method by the same authors, despite the title changing from Transformer-based to PLM-based models. The text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MTEB and LongEmbed evaluations, query/document ablations, and length- and temperature-dependent embedding analyses, including Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds STS diagnostics, LLM embedding measurements in Appendix D, and alternative-method evaluations in Appendix E.

M1.justification: TempScale still divides attention logits by a temperature before softmax, using the same formula in v1 Section 3 and v2 Section 4. Per-task temperature selection changes the evaluation protocol; the new comparator implementations do not change the proposed method.

E1.justification: Main benchmark coverage expands from 36 MTEB datasets plus four LongEmbed datasets to 39 plus four, adding SCIDOCS retrieval, FiQA2018 financial retrieval, and Touche2020 argument retrieval. SCIDOCS already appeared in v1's similarity diagnostic, so its retrieval task is the addition. Appendix D also adds LongRAG nq/hotpotqa and LongAlpaca-12k for long-text embedding diagnostics.

E2.justification: The five original embedding backbones remain. v2 additionally evaluates the reported last2avg variant of Flow and Whitening in Table 6, and Chiang and Cholak's Method1 plus an adapted YaRN scaling rule in Table 7. These introduce substantial comparisons with alternative mitigation approaches; full trained Flow and unmodified YaRN are not what these experiments evaluate.

E3.justification: v1 selects one optimal temperature per model across all tasks; v2 selects it per task, retaining the search grid. Table 1 also changes aggregation: v1 BGE's 0.51% matches the relative gain in its average score, whereas v2's 1.01% averages taskwise gains; its average score increases about 0.70%. New protocols include LLM diagnostics in 1,000-token bins, longest/shortest 10% ranking distributions, and a five-value YaRN parameter sweep.

E4.justification: v2 adds ranking-distribution diagnostics in Figure 4, related/unrelated/random sentence comparisons in Table 3, and LLM collapse analyses in Appendix D. Conversely, v1 Table 2's query-versus-document scaling ablation is removed. Much of the earlier entropy, repeated-token, and temperature-sensitivity evidence survives in Appendix C and is relocated rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and averages without repeated-run counts, seed details, confidence intervals, empirical error bars, or significance tests. The additional result tables do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1's reported overall and LongEmbed relative improvements change from 0.53% and 0.82% to 0.94% and 1.10%. Individual entries also change, such as BGE plus TempScale's LongEmbed score from 38.35 to 38.73. Changed coverage, temperature selection, and aggregation prevent interpreting these as controlled performance gains. Tables 3–7 add substantial STS, LLM, and comparator outcomes, while the original query/document ablation results disappear.

T1.justification: The principal filtering bounds and their proofs remain substantially unchanged. Appendix B.3 revises Theorem 8 from an increasing-similarity statement to convergence of cosine similarity to one, adding explicit high-frequency decay and nonzero DC-norm assumptions while largely retaining the proof. Appendix E.1 also introduces the cited alignment/uniformity decomposition of InfoNCE. These are localized formal additions.

C1.justification: The central claims of length-induced collapse, its low-pass-filter explanation, and mitigation through TempScale remain. v2 refines the claimed mitigation mechanism toward balancing filtering rates across lengths, emphasizes TempScale as validation of the analysis, removes the explicit tuning-free description from the abstract and contributions, and revises the headline improvement claims.

C2.justification: New Section 3 develops task-specific explanations involving classification geometry, retrieval interference, and STS confusion. Appendix E adds interpretations of why contrastive learning and other corrections may fail, emphasizing consistency across lengths and possible distribution mismatches from length-dependent scaling. LLM limitations now distinguish observed collapse from the still-unresolved explanation for unidirectional attention. Some new STS interpretations are not consistently supported by Table 3.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project source-code link, identifies three LLM embedding models, and documents the last2avg choice, Whitening implementation, and adapted YaRN formula and parameter range. Existing checkpoint links and most dataset/metric instructions remain. However, Table 1 drops the selected temperature labels, and the default temperature of 0.8 is no longer stated; the new task-specific optima are not listed.

R1.justification: Beyond the largely retained related-work section, v2 substantially expands positioning against contrastive alignment/uniformity, Flow, Whitening, Chiang and Cholak's attention scaling, and YaRN. Appendix E explicitly distinguishes their motivations and applicability from TempScale. New LLM and long-text dataset references further broaden the research context; these are substantive additions beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, theoretical exposition, method motivation, and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. v2 introduces standalone performance-mechanism and discussion sections, separates limitations from the conclusion, and reorganizes the appendices: earlier experimental analyses move to Appendix C, while dataset and model documentation move to F and G.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column to a two-column layout, with extensive redistribution of figures, tables, and equations. Existing theoretical plots are merged into appendix figures. New displays include the three-part mechanism illustration, ranking histograms, STS table, LLM tables, and alternative-method tables. The original query/document ablation table is removed.

improvement.justification: The added LLM diagnostics, explicit alternative-method experiments, expanded research positioning, and code-access information make v2 more informative and easier to assess. The net gain is limited by the removed query/document ablation and reporting weaknesses: larger headline gains combine changed coverage, temperature selection, and aggregation, while Table 3 does not consistently support the new STS interpretation. These additions provide a modest overall improvement without establishing a substantial strengthening of the central method or theory.
